newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK unit trust Jan-Nov net sales hit record high.
newsitem.headline: HK unit trust Jan-Nov net sales hit record high.

text.p: Hong Kong's unit trust industry had record net sales of US$600.92 million from January-November 1996, 3.6 times higher than the same period of 1995, the Hong Kong Investment Funds Association (HKIFA) said on Monday.
Net redemptions of $125.56 million in November prevented the January-November inflow from reaching an even higher level, the HKIFA said in a statement.
In November, 11 sectors registered more redemptions than sales, it said. Only Hong Kong equity funds, single Asian country funds and international funds registered net inflows that month, it said.

Hong Kong equity funds reversed the October outflow and came first in net sales in November by attracting new money of $24.12 million, it said, adding it was the second time after August 1996 that equity funds topped the list of net inflows.

"Buoyed by the strong property market, the favourable U.S. presidential result and the continued strength of the Dow Jones, the Hang Seng Index soared to record high in November," said HKIFA chairman Andrew Lo.
"There were, on balance, more investors who were keen to capitalise on the boom in the market," Lo said.
Hong Kong equity funds attracted $77.76 million in the first 11 months of 1996, or 12.94 percent of the industry's total, he said.

In the January-November period, Asian funds that excluded Hong Kong and Japan funds attracted the highest net inflow of $179.8 million, or 29.92 percent of the total, followed by the international sector which attracted about 29 percent, the statement said.
Both sectors had registered net inflows in almost all of the months leading to November, it said.
Asia-Pacific Regional funds that included Hong Kong and excluded Japan had the highest net redemptions in November at $74.29 million, the statement said.
Lo attributed the high level of redemptions to profit-taking towards the end of the year, saying Asia-Pacific regional funds registered net sales in the first nine months of 1996.
